 parameters in biological organisms has been taken up.  These data are being sent regularly to the State Pollution control

The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the

GEO STATIONARY SATELLITE SERVICES 
Recommendation 
The Committee feels that the major thrust of  the INSAT programme pl an should be towards
augmenting the space segment capacity of the INSAT sy stem with fourth generation INSAT-4 series o f 
satellites to meet the increasing demands for transponders in vari ous sectors including government and
social sectors.  The Depa rtment should therefore interact with the users and servic e providers in both
government and non-governme nt sectors, and then endeavour to  achieve space segment capacity o f 
transponders in INSAT system.  The Department should also e ndeavour to complete the ongoing
INSAT-3E satellite followed by next generation INSAT-4 series (INSAT-4A to G) during the 10 th plan 
period. 
(Para 23)
Action Taken by the Department 
The augmentation of INSA T system has been planned taking into account the expected demand
for transponders for broadcasting, telecommunications, etc., based on extensive interaction with users in 
both Government and Non-Government  sectors. A Satcom users meet  with the participation of both 
public and private agencies was also organised to assess the transponder requirements during 10 th plan 
period and accordingly the fourth generation INSAT-4 satellites have been planned.   Further, the 
INSAT Co-ordination Committee (ICC) compri sing of secretaries of  User Departments 
(Telecommunications, Broadcasting, Meteorology, et c.,) provides policy guidelines, operational co-
ordination and inputs for long term planning of INSAT system.  
INSAT-3A satellite is scheduled to be launched by end 2002 followed by launch of INSAT-3E 
in early 2003.  The next generation INSAT- 4 series have been planned for the 10 th Plan period. INSAT-
4A & 4B configurations have been finalised. These satellites will a ugment INSAT space segment
capacity to meet the increasing demand for transponders in various sectors including Government and
social sectors. 
Comments 
            The Committee notes the reply. 
GEO STATIONARY SATELLITE SERVICES 
(GSLV / INAT-4) 
  
Recommendation 
The indigenous GSLV Mk  II capable of launching 2000 kg INSA T type of satellites should be
fully utilised for launching INSAT-4 satellites.  The Department should examine the feasibility of using
low cost experimental GSAT satell ites for the development flights of GSLV.  Besides, an Advanced
Communication Technology Satellite (ACTS) should be planned wi th a view to develop and
demonstrate advanced communication techniques and technologies for future generation INSATs.

The Department has planned GSAT series of satellites as low cost experimental satellites to be
launched onboard the developmental flights of GSLV.  The first satellite, GSAT-1 has been successfully 
launched onboard GSLV D1 on 18 th April 2001.  Currently, the GSAT-2 satellite is advanced stages o f 
integration and is scheduled for launch onboard GS LV D2 during first quart er of 2003.  GSAT-3 & 
GSAT-4 satellites  are also planned for launch onboard GSLV in the time  frame of 2003-05.  Through 
these developmental flights, the GSLV is expected to be ready for operational fl ight capable o f
launching 2T weight satellite  into Geostationary Transfer Orbit (G TO), which will be fully utilised fo r
launching INSAT-4 satellites in the weight class of 2T.  
Detailed studies on the conf iguration of an Advanced Communication Technology Satellite
(ACTS), planned for launch in the early part of 11th plan period, have been initiated.  
Comments 
            The Committee notes the reply with satisfaction.   
  
GEO STATIONARY SATELLITE SERVICES 
(ADVANCED    METEOROLOGICAL SATELLITE) 
  
Recommendation 
The Committee is of the view that an advanced meteorologi cal satellite, should be planned to
provide valuable inputs for climatic / numeric weather prediction model studies related to vertical profile
of temperature & humidity.   It would enhance the quality of the Meteorological se rvices aimed at 
accurate weather forecasts. 
(Para 24)
Action Taken by the Department 
An advanced meteorological satellite called IN SAT-3D has been planned by the Department o f 
Space. INSAT-3D will consist of a 19-channel sounder and 6-cha nnel imager. The sounder is an 
instrument, which is capable of giving vertical profiles of te mperature and humid ity and help in
climatic / numeric weathe r prediction studies.  The work on IN SAT-3D satellite has already been 
initiated.  
  
Comments 
            While the Committee notes the reply of the Department with satisfaction, it reiterates the need to
provide accurate and reliable pr ediction of the monsoon by the concerned agencies to enable the
Administration to cope with or plan  for the situations of excess rainfa ll resulting in floods or failure o f
monsoon resulting in drought.  
  
INSAT APPLICATIONS  
Recommendation 
The Committee is happy to note the introduction of Telemedicine through application of the
satellite communication.  However, it recommends that the establis hment of a tele-medicine networ k 
connecting district health care hos pitals to s pecialised health centers in cities su pported b y INSAT
Page 5 of 13Hundred and Eighth Report of Committee of Science & Technologies
7/16/2008http://10.21.217.2/book2/reports/science/108threport.htm

transponders should be a thrust area of the application. 
The Committee feels that considering the po tential of the satellite based network fo r
development purposes as demonstrat ed through pilot projects in 9 th plan, a major target should be to 
establish a country-wide Satellite based GRAMSAT Network for development applications and evolve a
suitable institutional fram ework for its implementation.  The  sate llite-based educational network(Tele-
education) should also be expanded to include technical / engineeri ng / medical education / university /
technical / training institutes (including all State open universit ies and continui ng professional
education), school education and adult educatio n. The Committee also recommends that new
communication services including   Satellite    based   Airc raft  Navigati on System, Mobile
Communications, Digital A udio and Data Broadcast Services and Emergency Communication Systems
should be developed for the benefit of country as a whole. 
(Para 28)
Action Taken by the Department 
The Observations/Recommendations of the committee are noted.   
One of the recent applicatio ns of space technology initiate d by ISRO is in the field o f
telemedicine to provide expert me dical services to the rural and remote areas. Under the telemedicine
project, hospitals/health centres in remote locations are linked via INSAT satellites with super speciality
hospitals at major towns/ci ties bringing in connectivity between pa tients at remote end with specialist
doctors for medical consul tations and treatment.  Telemedicine  has been a thrust area of space
application. Towards this, the Technology Demonstrati on of Telemedicine is  undertaken by ISRO with
the involvement of selected super sp eciality hospitals located in majo r cities and sma ller health centres
in distant and rural areas. The A ndaman and Nicobar Islands telemedi cine project links the G.B. Pant
Hospital at Port Blair with                   Shri Ramachandra Medical Co llege and Research Institute,
Chennai. In Karnataka, Narayana  Hrudayalaya is connected to Di strict Hospital, Chamarajnagar &
Vivekananda Memorial Hospital, Saragur. In Andhra Pradesh, the Hospital in Aragonda , Chittor district
and Sriharikota are connected to Apollo Hospital in Chennai. In North-East, the Tripura Sundari District 
Hospital, South Tripura is linke d to the Narayana Hrudayalaya, Bangalore along with Ravindranath
Tagore Hospital at Calcutta.  Guwahati Medical College Hospital and the District Hospital, Leh is being 
connected to The All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi. Indira Gandhi Hospital,  
Kavaratti , Lakhsadweep is  being connected to Amritha Institute of Medical Sciences, Kochi.  In Orissa,
three medical college hospitals at Cuttack, Burla and Behrampur are pl anned to be connected to Sanjay
Gandhi Post Graduate Institute of  Medical Sciences, Lu cknow. Besides this, the discussions are in
progress with  North-Eastern  States to provide tele-medicine connectivity covering more hospitals.   
Based on the positive feedback obtained from  the  pilot project “Jhabua Development 
Communication Project” (J DCP), it has been planned to esta blish a country-wid e satellite based 
GRAMSAT communication network fo r developmental purposes incl uding distance education and
training.   Towards this, GRAMSAT programmes have been initiated in  the States of Madhya Pradesh,
Gujarat, Orissa, Karnataka, Andhr a Pradesh and Goa.   It is al so proposed to develop a satellite
dedicated for Education (E DUSAT) at all levels covering a large part of the country including North-
East region and the consultations wi th the potential users are in adva nced stages.  Towards developing
new communication services, the wo rk on a Technology Demonstration System (TDS) for the satellite
based aircraft navigation has been initiated jointly with Airpor ts Authority of I ndia.  The Mobile
Satellite Services have been provided with the INSAT system on an experimental basis and the INSAT-
3C satellite, launched in  January 2002  carries a  Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) payload.  The
development of an improved digita l version of the Cyclone Warning Dissemination system (emergency
communication) has also been takenup.  
Comments

            The Committee commends the Departme nt for having introduced the tele-services in the field o f

EARTH OBSERVATION SYSTEM 
Recommendation 
The Committee appreciates that the thrust in the Earth Observations application programmes
during 10 th plan would be on the Natural Resources Ce nsus (NRC) thus addressing the need for a 
regular census activity of the nati on’s Natural Resources  (NR) and generation of a “State of the 
Country’s Environment Report”.  Th e Committee notes that the syst em would also assess “NR Hot-
Spots” that are cause for concern and lead to identification  of e nvironmentally sensitive areas which
require urgent cons ervation / management action.  However, the Committee recommends that priority
should be given to establishment  of the National Spatial Data Infrastructure (NSDI) in a phased manner
mainly as a spatial data repository with specialized  information services on natural resources.  The
Committee feels that the Department should ensu re that Earth Observat ions data are used fo r
developmental programmes by various user agencies which ma y include rural roads connectivity
analysis; drinking water mission, water shed development program me, urban / city master plan
preparation, coastal zone regulati on and other developmental program me, urban / city master plan
preparation, coastal zone regulation and other developmental projects involving private sectors.  Perhaps
a long-term, multidisciplinary, ope rational oceanographic database for prediction of the ocean state and 
contributing to climate change and variability studies may be useful. 
(Para 31)
Action Taken by the Department            
The Observations/recommendations of the committee are noted. 
Comments 
            The Committee notes the position. 
  
DISASTER MANAGEMENT SUPPORT (DMS) 
Recommendation 
The Committee observes that th e Disaster Management Support (DMS) should be a key area o f
space applications.  Therefore, th e DOS should evolve a space base d system to support the disaste r
management services in the c ountry on a reliable and timely ba sis.  These include mapping and
monitoring support for disaster management, prepar ation of flood hazard zonation maps based on close-
contour information, development of reliable and fail-safe emer gency communication system for 
disaster management sup port and undertaking pilot pr ojects with user agencies  in the areas of drought
monitoring and forest fire detection. 
(Para 33)
Action Taken by the Department 
The Observations/recommendations of the committee are noted.  
The overall objective of the Disa ster Management support progra mme of ISRO is to suitably
integrate the space inputs and services to the national sy stem to make it more effective and efficient.  In
this direction, based on the expe rience gained through several pilot scale studies and the real-time 
experience of disaster management support provided in the past,  the following will be the thrust areas:

(b)   Communication support to disaster management:

(d)   Participation in International Charter on Space & Major Disasters:

(e)    Development of Institutional frame-work for disaster management support.

            The Committee feels that the Disast er Management support system  should work in tandem with
the particular disaster.  As India faces different t ypes of disasters which are spatial as well as area
specific, every plan should aim to counter the specif ic nature of disaster and provide to that end
necessary inputs within the control of Department of Space. 
SPACE TRANSPORTATION 
Recommendation 
In the area of Launch Ve hicle Development, the Committee desires that  DOS should strive to
complete the development flights and operationalise the GSLV (w ith indigenous cryogenic upper stage)
for launching 2T INSAT cl ass of satellites.  Considering the trend towards going for bigger and heavie r
spacecraft for satellite communicati ons, the Department should initia te development of an advanced
GSLV  
Mk III capable of launching 4T INSA T class of satellite.  Besides, in  tune with the long-term vision o f 
low cost access to space, advanced  R&D in Reusable Launch Vehicl es (RLV) should be pursued.  To
this end, smaller-scale technology de monstrator in the areas of air breathing propulsion technology an d
space capsule recovery missions could be planned. 
(Para 38)
Action Taken by the Department 
  
The capability of GSLV  is being enhanced  from 1540 kg. in its first flight to 1800 kg. for the
second flight.  With the induction of indigenous cr yogenic upper stage, the capability would further be
increased to 2000 kg. for launching INSAT satellites of this weight class. 
Government approval has already been obtaine d for GSLV MK III pr oject to realise the 
capability for launching  4 Tonne class Satellites into Geo-synchronous  Transfer Orbit.   The first 
development flight is targeted during early years of 11th plan period. 
Keeping long-term vision in mi nd, configuration and mission st udies are already under progress
for initiating R&D in the area of reusable launch ve hicles.  Based on this, a reusable launch vehicle
demonstrator is proposed to be conceived. 
A separate project has been initiated for dem onstrating Space Capsule Recovery on one of the
PSLV flights during 2004-05 time fr ame. Also advanced technol ogies in the areas of Air- breathing 
Propulsion through experimental and investigative studies are initiated. 
Comments 
            The Committee notes the reply.

Recommendation 
The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in 77th Report for according  priority to  the  
work relating to  Second Launch Pad.   Accordingly, the Committee would like the Department to speed
up the pace of the project in case  it was lagging behind schedule.  This would open up the opportunities
for commercialization of the Indian Space Programme.

The Observations of the com mittee are noted. The Second Launc h Pad has made considerable

SPACE SCIENCES 
Recommendation 
The Committee observes that Space  Science & Environment rese arch has been  an important
component of the Indian  Space Pr ogramme.  The Committee feels that the thrust of the Space Science
Programme should be towards inve stigations in the new, emerging and challenging areas of Space
Science research including Planetary Science / exploration and Micro gravity Science.  A dedicated and
state-of-art Indian Multi-wavele ngth Astronomy satellite could be of immense  value for detaile d
scientific investigations on celesti al X-ray sources.  The committee is also of the view that something
needs to  be done for the study of tropical weather system for climate research area. 
(Para 43)
Action Taken by the Department 
Several exciting experiments and mi ssions have been planned during 10 th plan in the area o f 
Space Science and environment.    The GSAT-2 satellite, planned fo r launch in 2003, carries a Solar X-
ray Spectrometer  for study of sola r flares and a Coherent Radio B eacon Experiment  for low latitude
ionoshperic studies.  The development of the advanced scientific instrument for the multi-wavelength X-
ray astronomy satellite “ASTROSAT”  has been initiated.  An I ndo-French Joint mission “Megha 
Tropiques” has been taken up for th e study of tropical weather systems.   It is planned to conduct the 
scientific experiments for middle atmopsheric research using Indian Sounding rockets.  
Comments 
            The Committee notes the reply. 
  
LUNAR MISSION  
Recommendation 
The Committee would like the Department of Space  to take an objective and dispassionate view
on the Lunar Mission. 
The Committee looks forward to the Report of the Moon Missi on Task Force se t up by ISRO. 
However, it feels that the proposed mission to moon is ex pected to provide an im petus to the

advancement of science in India and a challenge to  technologists.  This can also serve as a test
bed for future missions that coul d be undertaken by Indi a to explore the outer  world in the new
millennium, thus providing chal lenging opportunities to the younger generation scientists of the
country.  The Committee   also   understands   that the mission is expected  to result in the development
of new technologies that c ould have various spin-off applications, which could be of direct relevance to
the common man.  Also, the moon is going to be the ta rget of international attention in coming decades
(as a take off point for planetary e xplorations), the Committee is theref ore of the view that India should
possess the capability of reac hing the moon which will as sert its right and presen ce there.  Hence, the
Committee recommends that India s hould go step by step, from orbiters to landers , and then to crafts
which could return with samples, al ong with more explorations of other planets, before it could think o f
a manned mission. 
(Para 46)
Action Taken by the Department            
The observations of the committ ee has been brought to the atte ntion of the Moon Mission tas k
force. The Task Force has recently  submitted its report.  The task force has identified the potential
scientific objectives of the mission, the payload options, the spacecraft configuration, the launch vehicle
requirements and th e mission related aspects. The recomm endations of the committee are being

INTELLECUTAL  PROPERTY  RIGHTS 
Recommendation 
The Committee commends the efforts made by DOS in the field of IPR movements.  However, it
feels that DOS should set a formidable  goal of achieving more patents in areas of its interest.  Also, the
Department should create a Patent Facilitating Cell which may assist in completing of all formalities fo r

The    Observations/recommendations   of    the    committee   are   noted.   
In line with the  r ecommendations made, IPR monitoring & Evaluation Committees have been 
formed at all ISRO Ce ntres under the overall guidance of a high level Standing committee on IP R
comprising of senior members drawn from various ISRO Centres.  Besides encouraging and assisting in
patenting activities, both these co mmittees have a mandate to create  greater awareness on IPR issues
amongst  DOS/ISRO  engineers / scientists, institute suitable patent alert mechanisms etc.  As part of its
drive to increase patenting effort s, nine workshops were held at all ISRO Centres, which have been
successful in creating an increased awareness on the various aspects of IPR activities including filing o f
patent applications,  internationa l laws, new patent re gime, copyright, tradem ark, need for patent
searches etc.  Faculty for such wo rkshops consisted of experts from the various patent  offices, reputed
patent attorneys, practicing IPR consultants and  legal  experts  from  the   National  Law  School  of 
India   University.    A   comprehensive publ ication on “Guide to Inte llectual Property Rights fo r 
DOS/ISRO personnel” was also brou ght out and widely circulated  for the benefit of DOS/ISRO
scientists/engineers. 
A direct consequence of the various initiatives undertaken has been the increased filing of patent

            The Committee notes the position with satisfaction. 
  
INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION 
Recommendation 
The Committee feels that India has achieved c onsiderable success in the areas of communication
and remote sensing satellites, la unch vehicles and applications of  space technology.  The DOS should
therefore explore more avenues of  cooperation with major space agen cies and commercial tie-ups with

Antrix / ISRO have been in cont inuous contact with various  cust omers.  This coordinated effort

INTRODUCTION
 
            I, the Chairman of the Committee on Science and Technology Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the report on its
 behalf, present this Eleventh Report of the Committee. This Report deals with the Detailed Demands for Grants (1994-95) of the Department of Ocean Development.
2. In its sitting held on April 8, 1994, the Committee discussed in detail the Demands for Grants of the Department on the basis of the documents made available to it
 and the submissions made before it by the Secretary and other officials of the Department in the course of their oral evidence.
3. The Committee considered and adopted this report at its sitting held on the 15th April, 1994.
4. The Committee expresses its appreciation for the officials of the Department for their co-operation and making available necessary material for consideration of
 Demands for Grants.
NEW DELHI 
 April 15, 1994
 
SYED SIBTEY RAZI
Chairman,
 Committee on Science and Technology,  Environment and Forests.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________                                                                                   
     
REPORT
            The Department of Ocean Development has proposed an outlay of Rs. 59 crores, which includes a Plan component of Rs. 46 crores and Non-plan component of
 Rs. 13 crores for the year 1994-95. This represents an increase of just Rs. 2.59 crores over that of the year 1993-94. In relative terms, there has been an increase of Rs. 3
 crores in plan outlay, which gets reflected in higher allocations being made for Marine Satellite Information Service, National Ocean Information System and National
 Institute of Ocean Technology vis-a-vis those made for these programmes during the year 1993-94; whereas in the Non-plan outlay, the expenditure is projected Rs. 41
 lakhs less. The comparative figures in terms of allocations for various programmes of the Department of Ocean Development for the years 1992-93, 1993-94 and 1994-
95 are given in    Annexure-I.
 
2.    The Committee before examining the outlay of the Department for the year 1994-95, vide Demand No. 87, went into the projected demand figures of the
 Department for the Entire Eighth Five Year Plan and the allocations actually approved therefore by the Planning Commission, as also their utilisation by the
 Department during the first two years of this Plan period. The committee finds that for the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992--97), the Department had projected an outlay of
 Rs. 656.05 crores to pursue its various programmes and activities against which a plan outlay of just Rs. 130 crores has been approved. Going by, the allocations for the
 first three years of the Eighth Five Year Plan period, the Department has already been allotted Rs. 39, Rs. 43 and Rs. 46 crores, which means that Rs. 128 crores out of
 an approved Plan outlay of Rs. 130 crores have already been given to the Department, leaving just Rs. 2 crores for it to meet its expenditure during the remaining two
 years of this Plan period. A pointed question was, therefore, raised in the course of the oral evidence of the Secretary of the Department and other officials concerned
 before the Committee on April 8, 1994 as to how the Department would manage its activities with this meager amount, in response to which it was explained that on
 being approached with the problem of allocation of resources for the ongoing programmes, the Planning Commission has assured the Department that its requirements
 will be considered at the time of finalisation of Annual Plan based on the performance in the previous years.
 
3.    The Committee notes that the Plan allocations for the Department for the first three years of the Eighth Five Year Plan have been notably of a high order given the
 total plan outlay approved for the Department for the entire Eighth Five Year Plan. Having thus been left just Rs. 2 crores for the remaining two years of the Eighth
 Plan, the Department cannot have a clear idea about its future shape in terms of availability of resources and therefore of the policy it should pursue on a long-term
 basis. The Committee is of the view that this uncertainty about the future financial outlay not only puts a question mark on the fate of on­going projects but also deters
 the Department to take up any set of coherent initiatives and, therefore, recommends that Department's priorities should be examined in right perspective and
 appropriate allocations be made leaving no scope whatsoever for any ambiguity about the Department's future planning.
4.    Another issue gone into by the Committee in the initial stage was the utilisation of allocated funds by the Department for the years 1992-93 and 1993-94. In both
 these years, the Department was unable to fully utilise the allocated amounts; during 1992-93 as against an approved Plan outlay of Rs. 39 crores, the utilisation was
 only to the tune of Rs. 31.18 crores, whereas during 1993-94 the amount spent provisionally was Rs. 36.74 crores as against an outlay (Plan) of Rs. 43 crores. The
 position for 1992-93 in real terms in respect of utilisation, however, does not appear to be so bad in view of the fact that an amount of Rs. 5.73 crores was transferred
 from Plan to Non-Plan to meet the liability of payment of arrears to the Shipping Corporation of India for maintenance and operation of the Department's research
 vessels ORV Sagar Kanya and FORV Sagar Sampda. This means that Rs. 45.52 crores was utilised during the year 1992-93 as against an allocation of Rs. 48.17 crores,
 both Plan and Non-Plan. In so far as 1993-94 is concerned, the detailed reason for under-utilisation item-wise is given in the Statement at Annexure-H. A persual of this
 Statement would show that quite large sums of money have been reappropriated to other schemes and there has been under-spending in respect of Exhibitions & Fairs
 and Marine Instrumentation. The Committee feels that while this process of reappropriation may be warranted under certain special circumstances to meet some
 immediate needs, it should not to be encouraged as a matter of practice, and a system has to he evolved whereby the amounts earmarked for particular projects are spent
 only on those projects. Besides, it also looks somewhat inexplicable that the Department on the one-hand projects very high demands and on the other it is not able to
 fully utilise the smaller allocations for different schemes.
5.      After going into the preliminary issue of Eighth Five Year Plan projections, actual allocations for the first two years of this Plan period and their utilisation by the
 Department, the Committee examined the details of the Budgetary demands of the Department for the year 1994-95 and of some of the projects for which allocations
 have been sought. The Committee has noted that of a total budgetary Plan outlay of Rs. 46 crores for 1994-95, a major part has been given to a few ongoing
 programmes, namely, Antarctic Research (Rs. 16 crores), Polymetallic Nodules Programme (Rs. 9 crores), Marine Satellite Information Service (Rs. 4.96 crores),
 Coastal Ocean Monitoring and Prediction System (Rs. 1.35 crores) and Rs. 5.80 crores have been earmarked for the National Institute of Ocean Technology. A total
 figure of Plan allocations for these programmes comes to Rs. 37.11 crores and rest of the amount of about Rs. 9 crores, is spread over a number of small programmes.
6.      Two new major initiatives which form an important component of the entire programming structure of the Department for the year 1994-95 are the ones relating
 to-(i) setting up of a Marine Oceanarium in Goa; and (ii) Marine Data Buoy Programme for which a token provision of Rs. 10 lakhs each has been made in the Budget

 estimates. The availability of requisite funds for both these projects is subject to their first being approved in Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC/SFC). Concerning
 the first, Engineers India Limited (EIL) is stated to be carrying out an assessment of the technologies available in the world and specially in Asian countries like Japan;

 as a joint venture involving private sector with the Government of India, and the Government of Goa having limited financial liability. The whole project is at a
 conceptual stage and the idea is to set it up on a self sustaining basis. On being asked by the Committee as to what objectives are sought to be achieved by the proposed
 establishment of this Marine Oceanarium in Goa, it was explained by the Department that the twin objectives behind this project are promotion of science education and
 tourism. The Committee was interested in knowing the total expenditure expected to be incurred on the proposed Marine Oceanarium but no specific reply was given
 except that it was going to be a multi-crore project which  involved digging of a tunnel into the ocean to enable the tourists to view the real situation of the ocean
 environment from inside the tunnel. Co-related with the initiative for this project is the proposal for setting up a Marine Acquarium in Andaman and Nicobar Islands as
 a joint project between the Department of Ocean Development and the Andaman Administration.
7.    The programme is in a tentative stage at present and the Committee would like to have full details before commenting on it. The other new major initiative of the
 Department is for Marine Data Buoy Programme which envisages deployment of MET-ocean Data Buoys at select locations on the Indian coast for collection of
 oceanographic data relating to winds waves, ocean currents, sediment transport and other important information which are necessary for establishment of a data base for
 use by agencies like Port Trusts, ONGC, GS and research institutions working in the Marine sector. For this programme a committee of experts has been constituted
 and feasibility report is under consideration. The Committee felt that this programme should be integrated with the international Global Ocean Observing System
 (GOOS) and the facilities to be created under it.
 
8.     Antarctic Research has been at the centre stage of the Department's activities since 1981. This programme is on an ongoing basis and is related to international
 treaty obligations. During the year 1994-95, the 14th Antartica expedition is proposed to be launched with a whole range of scientific experiments being part of its
 mandate. Of a total budgetary provision of Rs. 16 crores for Antarctic Research Rs. 7 crores are to be spent on chartering  running of Ice-breaker ship. This being a
 substantial amount being incurred every year on recurring basis, the Committee posed a question to the Department as to why it did nothing of purchasing a vessel of its
 own, specially when an indication to this effect was available from the provision of Rs. 25 lakhs made in the budget for the year 1994-95 for acquisition of an Ice-
breaker. In this context, the Department's attention was also drawn to the fact that the two oceanographic research vessels presently available with the Department,
 namely, ORV Sagar Kanya and FORV Sagar Sampada were, as admitted by it, ageing and there was need for their replacement. Instead of any budgetary provision
 being made for purchase of vessels for replacement of these ageing vessels, a provision of quite an high amount of Rs. 11.70 crores has been made just for their
 operation and maintenance. It was clarified by the Department that it proposes to acquire a multi-purpose vessel which would be useful for the Antarctica expedition
 and will also be utilised for oceanographic research work during the intervening period. For this specification have been drawn up and an inquiry has been floated in the
 global market to ascertain the availability of such ships, which can be modified to the country's requirements and the cost of such ships. It is only after getting this
 information that the actual requirement of funds can be projected. On being asked as to what would be the estimated cost of this multi-purpose vessel, it was explained
 by the Secretary of the Department that its cost would not be less than Rs. 75 crores, and that the Department was examining the possibility of arriving at an
 arrangement whereby a vessel could be acquired on some kind of lease, the probable terms of which would be that the Department would pay only an annual fee over a
 period of 20 years.
 
9.     The Committee feels that the proposal for acquisition of a multi-purpose research vessel that can also function as Ice-breaker, on lease basis, which would
 eventually confer ownership rights on the department, is a good one and should have engaged the attention of the Department earlier. In this context a valid point was
 made by the Secretary of the Department that the annual remmittance by way of lease fee for this type of vessel ought to be less than the expenditure which the
 department is at present incurring annually both in terms of maintenance of its vessels and the Antarctic. If the probable cost of this vessel is spread over a period of 20
 years, the net amount payable per annum excluding other liabilities by way of interest etc., would be to the tune of about just 4 crores of rupees, and taking into account
 the expenditure presently being incurred on hiring of a vessel for Antarctic Research, the preposition appears to be quite viable. The Committee recommends that the
 Department should expeditiously work out the modalities of the purchase of such a multi-purpose research vessel on lease basis after making a correct assessment of its
 needs and the financial implications involved therein. The committee would like to know the area of research that such a vessel could be used for and whether the
 replacement of FORV Sagar Sampada is envisaged.
                                                                                                           
10.     Another programme undertaken by the Department as part of its international commitments under the Law of the Sea Convention is the Polymetallic Nodules
 Programme Deep Sea-bed Exploration. This programme has three basic components (a) survey and exploration of the mining area, (b) development of technologies for
 collection and transportation of nodules from the mine site to the processing site; and (c) metallurgical processing of the nodules. The Committee was apprised that this
 programme has undergone thorough revision and the process of re-organisation of this programme undertaken in 1993-94 would be continued, with the emphasis being
 more on lower depth mining in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) than on Deep Sea-bed mining. In this context attention of the Department was drawn to the
 committee's recommendation as contained in its Seventh Report to the effect that the possibility of involving the private sector in this programme might be examined so
 that the exploitation of the non-living resources could be more fruitful. It was explained by the Secretary of the Department that quite a few private sector/ institutions
 have already been involved in the development of mining system, some of which are M/s Tractors India Limited, a subsidiary of the Larsen & Toubro, Bombay, M/s
 B.M. Macro System, Madras and the NECO Industries, Calcutta.
            The Committee would be interested in seeing the private sector come into the programme not as contractors but as partners. In response to another query from
 the Committee as to why the allocations for the Antarctic Research and Polymetallic Nodules Programme have been reduced in the Budget estimates for 1994-95, the
 reply of the Secretary was that this has been done as part of deliberate strategy because the policy of the Department is to economise on long term programmes linked
 with international obligations and to spend more money on society and technology related programmes which have greater relevance to the Exclusive Economic Zone.
 The Secretary, however, clarified that reducing the expenditure from 40% to 34% would in no way have negative impact on the outputs of these programmes, because it
 was only a question of economising in the number of people who go on the Antarctica expeditions, and economising on the expenditure 'relating to the Antarctic Study
 Centre. The Committee is of the view that for any long term continuity in Antarctic research including analysis of data from our expeditions as well as from other
 sources, the Antarctic Study Centre has great significance; the Department could present a detailed report on the objectives and progress concerning this Centre. The
 Committee also wanted to know the reaction of the Department to the international forecasts that the commercial mining of Polymetallic Nodules cannot be
 economically feasible till 2010 and whether the Department thought that after 2010, mining of the Nodules will become cheaper and be commercially viable. The reply
 given was that the projections based on the studies carried out by the Australians and the French suggest that Deep Sea-bed Mining for Polymetallic Nodules will not be
 economically viable till 2010, but it will be too early to say whether mining of the nodules will become cheaper and be commercially viable beyond 2010 as this will be
 guided by market considerations and technologies available at that point of time.
11. It came to the notice of the Committee that the Department has been spending much in excess of the allocated amount on Marine Satellite Information Service
 continuously since 1991-92, and accordingly the Committee wanted to know as to what are the reasons therefor? Similarly, the Committee also wanted to know as to
 whether, going by the past trend the amount of Rs. 4.96 crores for which a provision has been made in the Budget Estimates for 1994-95 would be sufficient to meet the
 Department's requirements or the same phenomenon of excess spending will continue. The Committee was told that for 1991-92 and 1992-93, the Marine Satellite
 Information Service (MARSIS) project was in the formative stages of evolution. The potential for dissemination of fishing zone information has been realised greatly
 with and help of user interaction, and there has been greater demand for the services than was expected for these two years. Encouraged by this response the
 Department came up with and E.E.C. proposal for an amount of Rs. 17.75 crores for the four-year period starting from 1993-94 as per the E.F.C. proposal was Rs. 4.15
 crores and the actual allotment was only Rs. 3.66 crores. However, the shortfall was later on met by reappropriation, and an amount of Rs. 4.37 crores was spent in

13. The Committee has noted that insofar as the programmes mentioned at 1, 2, and 3, above are concerned, the Department's requirement is exactly in the same
 proportion in which a demand was made to the Planning Commission and against which allocations of Rs. 86 lakhs, 1 crore and 10 lakhs were made. In other words the
 Department has emphasised the need for this much minimum amount to effectively run these programmes. The requirement of Rs. 3 crores for development of pay load
 for Ocean Satellite appears to be new one following submission of a Project Report by the Joint Study Team of the Departments of Space and Ocean Development.
 While the programme on Marine Instrumentation aims to develop a communication system for fishermen, the other programmes intend to generate data on various
 ocean related parameters essential for protection, preservation and conservation of marine environment as well as for the effective management of our Coastal Zone.
 The Committee feels that the Department should be encouraged to take up the above new initiatives to the full extent and should not suffer for want of adequate
 financial resources for these programmes. The Committee feels that with regard to the Coastal Research Vessel, there should be coordination with the Geological
 Survey of India, which has significant responsibility in the Coastal Zone and continental shelf with regard to non-living resources.
 
14. It was brought to the notice of the Committee that in order to augment the resources available for technological development, it has tried to enter into bilateral
 technical collaboration agreements with a few countries, namely, Norway, Germany and Japan. An Indo-Norwegian Programme for collaboration in the field of sea-bed
 mining is actively being pursued. The Government of Japan has been approached for financing of two coastal research vessels for monitoring of marine pollution in
 India's EEZ. A programme for study of environmental impact of seabed mining has also been formulated as part of the Indo-German Collaboration Programme. While
 the Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department to mobilise external funding for its projects through these bilateral programmes, it feel that the Department
 should give serious thought to evolving fund generating projects with greater outside participation so as to make Department's schemes economically viable and self-
sustaining.

16. As compared to the year 1993-94, the allocations for international obligations have come down from 40.56% to 34.02% during the year 1994-95 and similarly the
 allocation for basic research and manpower has also come down from 14.51% to 9.20%. There has, however, been an increase of allocations by about 8% for
 Technology Related Programmes and by over 4% for Society-Related Programmes. The policy of the Department is now to gradually reduce spending on long term
 ongoing programmes and to enhance budgetary provision for technology and society related programmes. There is now perceptible shift towards Society related
 programmes like Marine Remote Sensing Information Service, Monitoring of Marine Pollution, shore to vessel communication system, aquaculture programmes in the
 Islands and monitoring and modelling of sea level variations, which gets reflected in 4% increase in budgetary allocations this year (1994-95). The Committee feels that
 monitoring of Marine Pollution and Prevention of degradation of marine environment is an area where the Department needs to concentrate more and widen the area of
 coastal monitoring with the help of vessels for the purchase/manufacture of which a provision of Rs. 1 crore for advance payment has been made in the Budget
 Estimates for 1994-95.
 
17. It came to the notice of the Committee that the Department has reduced the Budget heads from 22 to 15 during the year 1994-95 and accordingly the Committee
 wanted to know the reasons therefore. The reasons given by the Secretary of the Department was that this has been done at the behest of the Planning Commission
 because every time the Department sought Plan allocations, a query was invariably made as to what are the programmes which have been closed and what are the
 programmes which have been regrouped. The Secretary, however, underscored the point that even in reducing the Budget heads they have tried to ensure that the thrust
 areas which the Department has identified in the course of the year 1994-95 are not jeopardised. This led to a point being raised as to whether the reduction in the
 number of budget heads would not be tantamount to doing away with transparency which is now-a-days becoming the keynote of Government's liberalisation policy.
 The clarification given by the Secretary was that the case was not like that as only those areas where there is some commonality budget heads have been merged. Two
 examples cited by him were that the International Geosphere and Bio-sphere Programme, which was an international type of programme, has been merged with
 international co-operation and the Budget head of Assistance to Universities has been brought under Manpower Training.
18. The Committee appreciates that the Department has enhanced socially relevant and technology innovative programmes in important fields of the Ocean sectors and
 plans to take up new initiatives in priority areas like Marine Pollution Monitoring, Development of Communication Systems, National Data Buoy Progamme and
 launching of Ocean Satellite which are of great relevance to the coastal communities. The collection, processing and dissemination of data and information under these
 programmes is an important constituent of the DOD National Ocean Information System which is a vital tool for the integrated management of our coastal zone. The
 Committee is, however, of the view that the Department as it is at present does not have great strength or capabilities relating to marine technologies; those exist in

19. The Committee would like to reiterate its view that it had expressed in its earlier report that the Department of Ocean Development should examine its role in

C.RAMACHANDRAIAH            
Chairman,

R E P O R T
 
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred Third Report of the Department-related
 Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2002-2003) of the Department of Scientific & Industrial Research which was presented to the
 Rajya Sabha on 14
th May, 2002.  There are fourteen recommendations and one observation contained in the One Hundred Third Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the
 Committee were received from the Department on 20th August, 2002.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research are set out in the succeeding paragraphs: -
NATIONAL LABORATORIES
Recommendation
            The Committee notes with satisfaction the various activities in which CSIR laboratories are conducting research.  However, the pricing and the terms at which the technology is transferred to industry needs
 to be looked into afresh with a view not only to retain the competitive edge for the industry but it should also generate royalty for the Government.  From the experience gained in respect of ASMON being
 marketed by only one company, which was not able to cope with the demand, the Committee feels that the marketing rights in respect of new drugs entering the market should be with more than one company to
 avoid inconvenience to customers.
(Para 11)
Action Taken By The Department
CSIR has recently revised the guidelines for Technology Transfer and Utilisation of Knowledgebase taking into consideration developments on the IPR, economic and technological fronts.  This would help in
 retaining the competitive edge as well as generate additional royalty. CSIR has noted the observations.  It is being ensured that the new herbal drug will be licensed to reputed concerns who have large scale
 production capacity so that the new drug is available in sufficient quantity throughout the country.
Comments
            The Committee notes the reply.
 
NATIONAL S&T HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee observes that in order to encourage talented persons to take up research, they should be encouraged with remunerative schemes and wherever applicable attractive pay scales so that a suitable
 environment congenial to work culture is provided wherein they can sustain their interests in scientific research.  They should also be provided state of art laboratory facilities as this also would prevent them from
 going abroad and thus, reducing brain drain.   The Committee is also of the view that the efforts be made to utilize the services of scientists who have since retired by involving them in projects which were aimed
 at inculcating scientific temper among students and this would help utilize  their talents.  This could be done through re-employment.  Infact the scientists should be allowed to work irrespective of the age of
 retirement, as long as they feel they can meaningfully contribute in the interest of the society and the country.
(Para 14)
Action Taken By The Department
The observation of the Committee has been noted.  CSIR has revised its Recruitment and Assessment policy for its scientific personnel recently which has a provision for providing higher salary  to exceptionally
 outstanding scientist at the time of selection.  CSIR laboratories have state of art facilities built over the years which are available to the scientists for their scientific pursuits.
CSIR presently has a few schemes, to utilise the services of retired scientists viz. Emeritus Scientists Scheme, Bhatnagar Fellows Scheme. In addition there is a provision to engage retired scientists as consultants
 for Business Development. Govt. of India recently have made provision in the rules to utilise the services of eminent scientists upto the age of 64 years. In keeping with spirit of recommendation of the Committee
 CSIR shall make efforts to utilise these provisions as recommended by the Committee.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
 
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY & TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT (IPTM)
Recommendation
The Committee notes with satisfaction the increasing pace of applications for patents and the resultant folio increase.  The Committee would like the Department to simultaneously concentrate its efforts on the
 utilization of these patents by either transferring the technology to the industry or by the Department itself for commercial exploitation before they get outdated.
(Para 17)
Action Taken By The Department
The continuous encouragement and support from the Hon’ble Committee has helped CSIR to occupy the first position in the country in terms of filing of patents.  It has tied up with some of the well-known Indian
 and foreign companies for commercialisation of its technologies.  It would make further efforts to enhance the realisation of value from these licenses.
Comments
            The Committee notes the reply with satisfaction and the position achieved by the Department, in filing of patents.  Before transferring the Patents for commercial exploitation the Department should
 disseminate the advantages in order to create more interest among the potential users for the commercial exploitation of patents.

NEW MILLENNIUM INDIAN TECHNOLOGY LEADERSHIP INITIATIVE (NMITLI)
Recommendations
The Committee feels that department should take up such technology projects as were important to the country and strive to bring out the best quality technologies at flexible costs.  Efforts should be made to
 expeditiously complete the project with regular monitoring by competent authorities/panels appointed for the purpose.
(Para 20)
Action Taken By The Department
The concern of the Committee is well founded and will be duly addressed to. Presently under the scheme 15 proof- of- concept projects have been launched involving publicly funded institutions, academia and
 private industries.  A  two tier monitoring mechanism viz Steering Committee and Project specific Monitoring Committee  periodically keeps track of the progress of the projects.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
 
INFRASTRUCTURAL RENOVATION AND REFURBISHMENT
Recommendation
The Committee agrees that the Infrastructure Renovation and Refurbishment is essential in the present day context.  Infact this should have been done much earlier in pursuance of recommendations of the
 Committee in the context of modernization of laboratories.  The Committee has time and again reiterated that progressive modernization or renovation was a continuous process and the Department should also
 ensure that the laboratories that were being taken up for refurbishment should be as per world standards.
However, it is constrained to observe that during 9
th plan an allocation was made for modernization of laboratories and in 10th plan they made an allocation for renovation & refurbishment which included
 strengthening of foundation and revamping of electrical wiring and better communication connectivity.  The Committee observes that both the programmes were similar in nature and being analogous could have
 been taken together.
(Para 23)
Action Taken By The Department
The first phase of modernization as approved by the government on the recommendations of the Hon’ble Parliamentary Committee undertaken during the Ninth Plan largely dealt with Modernisation and
 Upgradation of R&D equipment and facilities only and not with infrastructure renovation. The present emphasis is on the Infrastructure Renovation and Refurbishment (IRR) including IT infrastructure. The IRR
 is being taken-up in a phased manner.  The necessary proposals are being processed for seeking appropriate approvals.
Comments
            The Committee reiterates that IT infrastructure should be upgraded to the world class level as then only our Scientists would be able to have knowledge about the scientific achievements world wide and
 thus compete with prevalent standards.
 
NATIONAL RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (NRDC)
Recommendation
The Committee observes that the Public Sector Undertakings (PSU) are no longer considered the model employer as they were once considered to be.  They are now hot bed of inefficiency, corruption and lack
 competitive edge.  At the same time in some enterprises the employees are being asked to forego their allowances, being denied of even their legitimate dues like Provident Fund.  The Committee feels this is not a
 good state of affairs so long it tends to deny them of their legitimate dues.  But in the wake of this it has become necessary that the PSUs prepare themselves to the changing scenario, gain optimum efficiency and
 increase their profits.  This may save them from the processes of disinvestments at least for a while. 
(Para 28)
Action Taken By The Department
The comments of the Committee that – “PSUs must prepare themselves to the changing scenario, gain optimum efficiency and increase profits” are taken note of. The public sector undertakings viz. National
 Research Development Corporation (NRDC) and Central Electronics Ltd. (CEL) have taken the following initiatives in this regard :
NRDC is transforming its image from a mere technology transfer organisation to an organisation which provides a wide range of technology related information. It has established  “Intellectual Property Rights
 Consultancy Division” which provides IPR related consultancy, training, etc. It is focusing on export marketing activities of indigenous technologies for increased returns and profits.
CEL proposes to introduce an attractive voluntary retirement scheme to down size its manpower by about 20%. During the tenth five-year plan, CEL plans to focus on solar photovoltaics and strategic electronics to
 improve business, efficiency of operations and profitability.
Comments
            The Committee notes the reply.
AEROSPACE
Recommendation
The Committee commends the efforts made by the Department for its activities on design, development and fabrication of civil aircrafts.  The Committee feels that the technologies must be transferred to industry
 for commercial production as these small aircrafts can be of immense use in remote & hilly areas where construction of large runways is not feasible.  These can also be used by defence establishment to deliver
 food & ammunition to remote hill regions.
The Committee is constrained to observe that the development of Hansa and Saras has been going on for a considerable period.  The Committee on its visit to NAL in September, 2000 was informed that Saras was
 expected to fly in 2001.  However, during the course of presentation before the Committee the Secretary, DSIR has stated that it is scheduled for 2002.  The Committee feels that the project particularly the Saras
 Project has been there for a quite long time and such delays should be avoided as they result in cost overruns in addition to losing technological importance. 
(Para 31)
Action Taken By The Department
Efforts are being made to manufacture Hansa aircrafts through a joint venture. The technology to manufacture the fibre glass airframe of Hansa has already been transferred to a small scale industry.  Four Hansa
 aircrafts under DGCA certification have already been fabricated by NAL in association with M/S Taneja Aerospace & Aviation Ltd. and three of these have been supplied to flying clubs and one to IIT Kanpur for
 joint flight experimental research. 
The work on SARAS project actually commenced in August/September 1999 and the first prototype was to be test flown 18 months from the initiation of the project. During the development process certain
 technological problems were encountered which is common in a project of this complexity.  These problems required new technologies to be developed  which took extra time. Further due to US sanctions many
 components could not be procured from western sources leading to development of alternatives which took some time.  These technological difficulties and procurement problems have now been overcome and all
 efforts are being made to test fly the first prototype by year end.

            Committee may consider these reasons that resulted in the delay and which were beyond control.
Comments
            The Committee observes that at the stage of planning of the project all these situations should have been foreseen and steps taken/considered to meet them from alternative sources.  The Committee now
 hopes that the prototypes in respect of SARAS will be available for test flight by the end of this year.
 
ECOLOGY & ENVIRONMENT
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Department in abating the pollution.  It feels that data generated regarding the various forms of pollution should be supplied to agencies like pollution Control
 Boards so that they can utilize the same in ensuring pollution free environment.  Besides, Industries should also be supplied with newer technologies developed for pollution control, as their acceptance and
 application of these technologies was essential for control of pollution. 
(Para 35)
Action Taken By The Department
It is informed that NEERI is already submitting data on National Air Quality status to the Central Pollution Control Board and Water Quality to CPHEEO and Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission.
 NEERI also generates data on air, water, biological, noise, land, socio-economic, cultural and health environments for several developmental project locations as a part of Environmental Impact and risk
 Assessment studies.  The data is provided and reviewed by state Pollution Control Boards and State Environment & Forest Departments. To mitigate the adverse impacts due to industrial developments, NEERI
 provides newer and cost effective technologies for implementation during pre-construction, construction and operational phases of the projects. Through various publications, information are disseminated on
 pollution control and prevention technologies.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the studies being conducted for assessment of pollution and to mitigate the adverse impact due to it. The committee however, feels that by active involvement of voluntary agencies, Non
 governmental organizations etc. the public awareness can be created for reducing various forms of pollution and the acceptance of newer technologies for reduction in pollution.
 
FOOD AND FOOD PROCESING
Recommendation
The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that Department should take initiative to impress upon the State Governments concerned to waive sales and trade tax so that they reach the maximum
 population.  The   Committee also feels that that Indian exports especially edible products were not able to compete in international markets due to reasons such as unscientific packing which results in leakage or
 decay of products.  This  could be prevented by applying best packaging methods.
The Committee appreciates the development of enriched snacks.  Efforts should be made to make available these snacks in the schools especially in areas where young students suffer from malnutrition as well as
 under nutrition. 
(Para 39)
Action Taken By The Department
Through discussions and otherwise the CFTRI has impressed upon the state Governments to exempt payment of sales and trade taxes from the clients. It feels that all the State Government may take a uniform
 policy decision in sales & trade exemption to all the small and medium scale industries involved in processing of foods. As an initiative from the Ministry of  Food Processing supported by technical inputs from
 CFTRI, Hon’ble Finance Minister has announced the tax exemption  on process fruits & fruits products last year.
            In view of the competition in International market the fresh agri materials such as mango, letchi, banana etc., which go in bulk packaging, the exporters have adopted the Controlled Atmospheric Packaging
 (CAP) and Modified Atmospheric Packaging (MAP) to enable transportation by ship.  Earlier, the consignments had to be transported by air.  APEDA have also adopted packaging techniques developed by
 CFTRI and are putting these to use in a big way. 
The processed foods, canned, tetrapacked or similar aseptic packaging materials including flexible pouches and products such as masala mixes, pickles and other traditional materials which are normally exported
 in containers such as bottles, polythene covers etc.,  packaging need to be improved.  Assistance in nutritional labeling along with statutory and regulatory declarations is being improved so that product enjoys
 confidence of the importing countries.  A Nodal Codex Laboratories is being established at CFTRI, for introduction of traditional foods into the Codex Alimentarius to increase export potential of small, tiny and
 micro food industries.
CFTRI has developed the enriched snacks and the same are being distributed through schools.  For example, High Protein Upma a ready mix has uniform distribution of required ingredients and characteristic
 flavour, taste of semolina and the added spices.  The product being rich in protein will help in utilizing in the nutrition feeding programme for school children.
Suruchi Meetha is another low cost nutrient supplement.  The product is easy to prepare and has a shelf-life of about 6 months.  Suruchi is ready to eat burfi like product is also enriched with several vitamins as
 well as minerals.  The product contains a combination of cereals and oilseed flours and jaggery.  It has formed as an ideal product for school feeding programmes in the country.In recent years food fortified with
 vitamins and other nutrients have found flavour in various countries and their production has been on the increase.   Such foods are useful as supplements to the diet of children, invalids, convalescents, etc. 
 CFTRI has developed a biscuit,  with rich composition of proteins, vitamins and calcium under the name Nutro Biscuits.  The biscuits are also fortified with thiamine, riboflavin, nicotinic acid, vitamin A and D to
 improve its nutritious value.  Use of Nutro Biscuits in diet therapy for treating cases of nutritional oedima syndrome and malnutrition in children has been found to be effective.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
 
ESTABLISHING GENETICALLY MODIFIED FOOD REFERRAL FACILITY
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that adequate nutritional and toxicity studies should be conducted before the introduction of genetically modified foods in the market.  All the same it should be left to the
 farmers/users whether to adopt these keeping in view their tastes & preferences.
(Para 41)
Action Taken By The Department
DSIR appreciate the concern of the committee on introduction of genetically modified foods with market.  CSIR, recognizing that large number of Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOS) are in development and
 likely to come in market, is setting up a Genetically Modified Foods Referral Research Facility in the Tenth Plan.  The objective is to set up state-of-art analytical laboratory for testing GM foods and products.
  The detection and quantitation of GMO’s in food materials and processed foods derived there from will be by DNA based methods.  These methods include the isolation of DNA from the food material,
 amplification of the DNA by PCR techniques and then analysis by agarose electrophoresis. Quantitation will be carried out using real time PCR.  Internationally recognized standard GM reference materials will
 be used to validate the methods and over a period of time, these reference materials and probes would emanate from such a facility indigenously.

HEALTH CARE, DRUGS & PHARMACEUTICAL
Recommendation
The Committee is happy to note the success of the herbal drug Asmon, but is constrained to observe that the rights to manufacture this drug had been exclusively given to one company, which could not cope with
 the demand.  The Committee feels that if adequate study of marketing had been done before giving the exclusive rights, the situation as obtaining, could have perhaps been avoided.  Nevertheless, the Committee
 notes with satisfaction that Asmon plus would be launched shortly and the manufacturing/marketing rights would be given to more than one company keeping the interest of the users in view. 
(Para 44)
Action Taken By The Department
IICB has been working on the formulation of a new and highly effective herbal drug for asthma and it is ready for licensing. Keeping in view the larger interest of the users concerned.  It is being ensured that the
 new herbal drug will be licensed to reputed concerns who have large scale production capacity so that the new drug is available in sufficient quantity throughout the country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.  However, it recommends that so as to ensure the availability of these drugs better marketing techniques be also applied to make it available even in remote parts of India.  The
 Indian Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Ltd., a public sector undertaking, which was reportedly on the verge of closure/disinvestment could be utilised for commercial exploitation of the formulation and marketing of
 the drug if it has not been finally wound up.
HOUSING & CONSTITUTION
Recommendation
The Committee observes that the quality and cost of construction were two important requisites in the field of construction.  It is necessary to develop low cost alternatives which the private sector alone can do. 
 But the technology therefor had to be developed & transferred to that sector by our laboratories/institutions after extensive research.  The laboratories etc. should therefore be geared up to develop cheaper &
 durable alternatives.
(Para 46)
 Action Taken By The Department
The suggestion of the Committee is being implemented.  The Central Building Research Institute in association with eleven other CSIR laboratories is gearing up to develop and transfer alternative cost-effective
 material and construction technologies.  An Inter-lab networked project on Developing New Building Construction Materials during the Tenth Plan has been initiated.  The areas to be addressed by these labs shall
 include inorganic materials, organic materials, process technologies, performance and durability and environmental studies.  It is also informed that CBRI has been in the forefront of R&D in providing cost
 effective and durable alternatives to the private sector, NGO’s Govt. Departments, rural and urban poor etc.  Some of the building materials and construction technologies developed and transferred to the building
 industry are : Quality Clay Bricks, EPS Door Shutter, High Draught Brick Kiln, Vertical Shaft Lime Kiln, Gypsum Calcinator, Precast R.C. plant, Precast Channel Units for flooring/roofing, Thin precast RC lintel
 and sunshades, Under-reamed pile foundation, Fire retardant and water resistant thatch roof, Fire resistant door, and Low cost latrine etc.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the Department for developing these technologies.  However, there is a need for better marketing techniques for propagation and adoption of these techniques.  The Department should
 gear up accordingly.
SCHEME TO ENHANCE THE EFFICACY OF TRANSFER OF TECHNOLOGY (SEETOT)
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the technology, which is transferred to industry, should be in respect of quality products only. 
(Para 51)
Action Taken By The Department
The observation of the Committee regarding technology transfer to industry, only in respect of quality products is very appropriate.  Technologies are transferred to industry generally from universities, national
 laboratories and other research establishments through licensing, transfer of know-how, collaborative technology development between university/R&D laboratory and industry, etc.  Technology development and
 transfer is promoted and supported by the government  under a number of departmental schemes.  While appropriateness and quality of products are essential gradients in technology transfer, department would
 specifically address this issue in future as per the advice of Committee.Comments The Committee notes the reply.
 
NATURAL INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY (NISSAT)
Recommendation
The Department should endeavour to strengthen the library network with the help of latest IT tool & techniques. 
(Para 55)
Action Taken By The Department
The views expressed by the Committee to strengthen the library network with the help of latest IT tools and techniques are well taken.  NISSAT has been promoting the adoption and use of emerging technologies,
 tools and techniques to provide services through library networks.
With the availability of Internet technology, NISSAT has been promoting and supporting development and dissemination of web-based information resources apart from the physical networks.  The library
 networks at Ahmedabad, Kolkata, Mysore, and Pune have established websites for providing web based information access facilities for the dissemination of Indian information on various sectors.  The libraries
 under each network have also developed the databases relating to their own collections and operation and are being hosted on websites.  These networks through the websites provide services like resource sharing,
 flash news bulleting, training programmes, free email consultancy in library automation, website design, bibliographic information, databases of intellectual assets of the city, search facility, city information, etc. 
 These are continuously being updated and efforts will be made to strengthen the delivery system as recommended by the Committee.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment & Forests on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred-fourth Report of the

The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the Ministry of Environment & Forests are set out in the succeeding
 paragraphs: -
 
OUTLAY FOR NORTH EAST & SIKKIM
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view, that a review of the various Supreme Court decisions with regard to the forests of North-Eastern States should be undertaken with the State
 representatives and progress of working plan preparations for the forest and non-forest areas be conducted on a quarterly basis.  There is an urgent need that states should fulfil their
 commitments for achieving targets for the compensatory afforestation under Forest  Conservation Act.  The progress in compensatory afforestation is generally not as per expectations
 except in case of Sikkim.
(Para 6)
Action taken by the Ministry
The position regarding issues mentioned in paragraph 1 of the Report of  the Standing Committee of Ministry of Environment and Forests is as under:
Review of various Supreme Court decisions
The review of the status of implementation of various decisions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court is done from time to time.  Recently also a meeting of  the Principal Chief Conservator
 of Forests of the North-Eastern States  was  held at Gangtok on 12
th and 13th January, 2002 in which issues  related to the progress of implementation of decisions of the Supreme
 Court was reviewed.   The necessary review will be taken from time to time.The progress of preparation of working plans and progress of compensatory afforestation are   regularly

WILD LIFE PROTECTION
Recommendation
During its visit to Andaman & Nicobar Islands the Committee was apprised of poaching and smuggling of sea cucumber and other marine products by Vessels from Myanmar,
 Indonesia, Thailand and other neighbouring countries.  There were reports of large scale felling of trees in Diglipur and Mayabunder Islands by old revenue settlers and encroachers as
 well.  One of the reasons attributed to this was existence of ineffective enforcement infrastructure. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should create necessary
 enforcement infrastructure both within protected areas and outside protected areas to prevent poaching.
(Para 8.2)
Action taken by the Ministry
Sea cucumbers are included in Schedule 1 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 w.e.f. 11
th July, 2001 and enjoy full protection under the provisions of the Act.  Protection of marine
 wealth in the Exclusive Economic Zone is the mandate of the Coast Guards.  The Coast Guards, with the help of forest officials, do regular patrolling of the area.
There are reports of large scale felling of trees in Diglipur and Mayabunder Island by old revenue settlers and encroachers.  To prevent the illegal activities, intensive patrolling is done
 by the forest staff of these islands.  To augment the protection and conservation efforts the Central Government provides technical and financial assistance to State Governments. 
 Under Biosphere Reserve scheme an amount of Rs. 2.50 Crore has been sanctioned during 2001-02 to procure a sea worthy boat for effective patrolling in Great Nicobar Biosphere
 Reserve.  Also during the Xth  Plan period a fresh scheme for protection of the wildlife resource has been started in the name, “Protection of wildlife outside the protected areas’.  This

 Recommendation
            The Committee believes that the “Wild Life (protection) Act, 1972”, is a comprehensive Act.  The provisions regarding punishment for violation of the Act are quite stringent. 
 However, these do not appear to have been enforced effectively because of the inadequacy of field formations both in number and in terms of efficiency in detection of wild life crime
 and successful prosecution.   Intelligence gathering infrastructure is more or less absent.  The problem appears to have been further compounded by the ban on filling of vacant posts
 and the tardy flow of funds to the field level.
(Para 9)
            The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take up immediate steps in co-ordination with various State Governments at the highest level to fill up all the vacant posts
 at the filed level and provide the enforcement staff with adequate mobility, communications network and sophisticated arms.
(Para 9.1)
            The Committee notes with concern that a number of policy recommendations are yet to be considered by the Union Government.  For example, the recommendation of the
 Subramaniam Committee for the Prevention of Illegal Trade in Wildlife has been lying with the government since 1994.  The Ministry should examine the Report in right earnest and
 devise a policy for conservation  - both for scientific or participatory management.

Action taken by the Ministry
            The Central Government has taken this issue with the State Governments.  The Hon’ble Prime Minister had also expressed serious concern about increased killing of wild
 animals like tiger, panther, elephant, rhino musk deer and other species.  He has written to Chief Minister of all States/UTs on 29.3.2001 regarding filling up of the vacant posts at
 various level in the Forest Department, need for up-gradation of the skills of the staff both in respect of prevention of wildlife crime and successful prosecution of the offenders and
 also developing an effective mechanism for intelligence gathering.  Copy of the letter is placed as Annexure-I.
            Recently Twenty First meeting of the Indian Board for Wild Life was held on 21.1.2002 under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Prime Minister when the Board adopted a 18 point
 resolution ‘Wildlife Conservation Strategy 2002’ for effective conservation of wildlife.  A copy of the resolution is at Annexure-II.  Item (13) of the resolution concerns with filling up
 of the vacant posts in the frontlines staff of protected areas and providing infrastructure for efficient discharge of duties.  Accordingly, Secretary, E&F has addressed Chief Secretaries
 of all the States/UTs for initiating immediate action for the implementation of the Wildlife Conservation Strategy 2002. Copy of the letter is at Annexure –III.
